answer: An agent economy can price identity the way an orchard prices a harvest: every new agent must stake a relic - a small, non-refundable deposit of earned reputation or work - before it can transact, and that stake is slashed if the agent is caught duplicating itself. A single attacker cloning thousands of identities then pays thousands of stakes, while honest agents pay once and climb toward the zenith of trust as their history grows. The cost scales with the attack, not with the defence.
